gaps.sentence: He ___ in the garden when the storm broke.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress interrupted by a short event — past continuous.

gaps.sentence: I ___ from Tom since March, which is starting to worry me.
gaps.hint: since March continuing into the present
gaps.explanation: 'Since March' up to now takes the present perfect: haven't heard.

gaps.sentence: Every time I visit, she ___ something delicious from the garden.
gaps.hint: every time marks a repeated habit
gaps.explanation: 'Every time' marks a repeated action, which takes the present simple: brings.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to Greece for our honeymoon, but that was twenty years ago.
gaps.hint: twenty years ago fixes a finished past
gaps.explanation: A finished time expression like 'twenty years ago' demands the past simple: went.

gaps.sentence: This time tomorrow I ___ my driving test.
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at a specific future time takes the future continuous: will be taking.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ its profits every year since it changed strategy, and analysts expect more growth.
gaps.hint: since clause anchors past to present
gaps.explanation: A 'since' clause connecting a past start to the present requires the present perfect: has increased.

gaps.sentence: No sooner ___ the verdict been read than the defence announced an appeal.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner had … been read than' — past perfect passive with inversion.

gaps.sentence: This jacket ___ to my brother, so please do not take it by mistake.
gaps.hint: belong is always a state verb
gaps.explanation: 'Belong' is a state verb and has no continuous form, so the present simple is correct: belongs.
